candidates.detail: Wardrobe::save validates and serializes its library before calling std::fs::write on the destination. The pinned locally installed Rust source defines fs::write as File::create followed by write_all; File::create opens with truncate(true), and the write_all loop can return an error after some writes. Thus an existing wardrobe file can already be truncated or partially replaced if an I/O error or interruption occurs after opening. Source reasoning only: no wardrobe file, save, fault injection, product or runtime ran.
candidates.consumer_and_safeguards: The studio Save to wardrobe and Delete actions clone the in-memory library, update the clone, save it, and assign it back only on success. A reported save error therefore leaves that in-memory library unchanged, but the direct destination write has no rollback of a file already truncated; later Wardrobe::load reads and validates the file and may fail or read incomplete data. Validation and serialization errors happen before the destination write. The default path is the studio wardrobe JSON, but no real user data loss, specific platform result, crash outcome or filesystem durability guarantee was observed.
